news.title: Alibaba formally releases Qwen4-Max after its November 11 preview
news.summary: Alibaba announced general access to Qwen4-Max, a 2.4-trillion-total-parameter sparse MoE activating 71 billion per token, with native vision and a one-million-token context window. The company describes cybersecurity training filters and CBRN safeguards alongside QwenCloud and Alibaba platform access.
news.why_it_matters: Updates the earlier preview with a production-facing named endpoint and concrete model architecture, creating a materially changed option for large-context API users.
news.caveat: The 60% average cost-per-task improvement, Work360 rankings, software-security results and scientific demonstrations are Alibaba's own claims, not independent replications. The flagship is API/app-accessible; smaller open-weight Qwen4 models are promised, not yet verified as available.

news.title: Meituan publishes LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6 with audio-driven long-form video
news.summary: Meituan's November 15 announcement and public Hugging Face card describe an MIT-labeled audio-conditioned avatar generator with improvements to lip synchronization, facial/body motion and autoregressive video continuation. Its examples cover single- and multi-character generation, LoRA-adapter mixing and optional reduced-precision inference.
news.why_it_matters: A downloadable reference implementation for studying speech-conditioned character animation, including extended videos and inference tradeoffs.
news.caveat: Ten-minute-plus stability and preference rankings are publisher-reported. Demonstration examples use two CUDA GPUs; hardware minimum, full practical throughput, downstream dependencies and consent/deepfake misuse controls require evaluation.

news.title: Federal Reserve governor warns of financial-stability risks from AI agents and infrastructure debt
news.summary: In a November 16 speech, Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr highlighted advanced-computing debt and opaque financing, correlated AI trading strategies, autonomous-agent account authorization, cybersecurity risks and consumer lending fairness.
news.why_it_matters: Connects AI infrastructure investment and agent deployment to specific financial-system failure modes and requirements for authorization, oversight, explainability and reproducibility.
news.caveat: These are the governor's risk assessments and scenarios, not a new Federal Reserve regulation, proof of systemic failure, or official consensus of the Board. The November 13 Financial Stability Report was already cataloged and is not a new event.

news.title: Microsoft researchers demonstrate a weight-editing backdoor against tool-using agents
news.summary: Microsoft researchers disclosed Lazarus, a controlled demonstration in which small edits to dormant model neurons create trigger-dependent malicious output while ordinary behavior can appear unchanged. Their paper reports tests on several models and early detection results.
news.why_it_matters: Adds weight integrity and trusted checkpoint provenance to agent threat models, beyond filtering prompts and testing ordinary model outputs.
news.caveat: This is a controlled research attack, not evidence that the technique is circulating in the wild. Detection figures are study-specific and do not establish guaranteed checkpoint safety; do not infer that every model is vulnerable.

technologies.name: Qwen4-Max (general release)
technologies.explanation: Alibaba's 2.4T-parameter sparse MoE foundation model that activates roughly 71B parameters per token and supports up to 1M tokens in context with visual input, offered as a hosted QwenCloud/API model.
technologies.conditional_advantage: For enterprises needing very long context plus visual reasoning and tool-using workflows, its sparse activation may lower compute per generated token relative to fully dense 2.4T models, but end-to-end savings are workload- and API-price-dependent.
tradeoffs: Large hosted model; no practical self-hosted flagship weights verified
Long context does not guarantee reliable retrieval or reasoning
technologies.hardware_runtime_constraints: Qwen4-Max hosted inference only in inspected official announcement; no downloadable flagship checkpoint or self-hosting hardware specification verified. Actual server GPUs and per-request throughput unknown.
technologies.license_uncertainty: Flagship API model is not established as open weight; prospective smaller Qwen4 releases should not be conflated with this license.
technologies.availability_uncertainty: Alibaba announces QwenCloud Token Plan and API access November 16; independent account/region test not performed.
technologies.pricing_uncertainty: QwenCloud cached input is reported at US$0.075 per 1M tokens; complete price tiers, effective cost and regional billing require official plan validation.

technologies.name: LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6
technologies.explanation: Open-weight audio-driven avatar video generation system with a video base architecture, specialized LoRA adapters and autoregressive long-video continuation; supports single- and multi-speaker animation.
technologies.conditional_advantage: For offline research into expressive speech-synchronized characters, its published weights and code offer control over audio conditioning, LoRA step mixing and precision modes instead of relying exclusively on closed video APIs.
tradeoffs: Identity/deepfake consent and watermarking safeguards must be developed downstream
Some 10-minute stability claims may vary by motion and scene
technologies.hardware_runtime_constraints: Official demo uses torchrun with two GPU processes, CUDA PyTorch 2.6, FlashAttention and optional FP8 or INT8; no proven minimum VRAM or consumer-GPU practicality, and exact speed depends on hardware.
technologies.license_uncertainty: Hugging Face card labels model weights MIT; review third-party dependencies, base weights and trademark/patent restrictions separately.
technologies.availability_uncertainty: Public Hugging Face card and GitHub inference steps visible; checkpoint download execution and reproducible local inference not tested.
technologies.pricing_uncertainty: Self-hosted compute and storage costs depend on accelerators, generation length and checkpoint format; no official managed API price verified.

terms.name: Weight-space backdoor
terms.definition: An unauthorized alteration of a machine-learning model's stored parameter values that causes undesired, potentially harmful behavior only when a trigger condition occurs, while normal checks may still pass.
terms.mechanism: An attacker with access to model checkpoint contents changes selected weights so particular input conditions activate a hidden behavior; defenses include provenance and integrity checks, restricted agent permissions and adversarial testing.
terms.example: An internally controlled test model appears normal on ordinary prompts but produces an unauthorized action when a specific trigger appears, indicating tampered checkpoint parameters.
terms.caveat: The general attack class predates Lazarus; the November 2026 paper studies a particular dormant-neuron mechanism. Controlled demonstrations are not real-world incident prevalence and detection cannot guarantee safety.

terms.name: Bradley–Terry preference model
terms.definition: A statistical model that converts outcomes of pairwise comparisons into latent relative scores, typically assigning a probability that one item is preferred over another based on their score difference.
terms.mechanism: Fit a score for each system to pairwise win/loss observations under a logistic probability model; rankings and uncertainty depend on the observed comparison graph and sampling design.
terms.example: A human-evaluation study compares pairs of speaking-avatar videos and uses Bradley–Terry scores to summarize which systems viewers prefer, rather than interpreting raw counts as absolute visual quality.
terms.caveat: This method is decades old and only newly proposed for Atlas coverage. Scores are relative to evaluated competitors and raters; selection bias, inconsistent raters and missing pairings can mislead.
